deep.reconstruction:
This page is Riemann's draft opening of 'Lehrsätze aus der analysis situs für die Theorie der Integrale von zweigliedrigen vollständigen Differentialien'. The section was published in Crelle's Journal 54 (1857) as part of the paper on Abelian functions. The previous page holds drafts of a cover letter and the title 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen'. The next page continues the published text.

(1) Motivation. Analysis situs (Leibniz's term, used here in a somewhat different sense) is the part of the theory of continuous magnitudes that ignores metric relations and studies only relations of place and region. A full, purely non-metric treatment is reserved for later. Here Riemann gives, in geometric dress, only the theorems needed to integrate exact differentials in two variables.

(2) Setting. T is a connected surface spread over the (x,y)-plane, possibly with several sheets. X and Y are continuous functions of position on T with X dx + Y dy exact everywhere, i.e. dX/dy - dY/dx = 0.

(3) Claim. Let A be any part of T. The integral of X dx + Y dy over the whole boundary of A is 0, provided the whole boundary is traversed consistently: always on the same side relative to the inward-to-outward normal.

(4) Reason, by Green/Stokes:
oint_{dA} (X dx + Y dy) = ± ∬_A (dX/dy - dY/dx) dT.
The sign is + for one orientation and - for the other. The integrand vanishes, so the boundary integral vanishes.

(5) Consequence (finished on the next page). The integral between two fixed points has the same value along two paths whenever the two paths together form the full boundary of a part of T. This leads to the definition of simply connected surfaces and to making a surface simply connected by cross-cuts (Querschnitte).

Right-margin jottings belong to different material. They mention functions that become infinite or infinitely small only of the first order, a relation t2 = -α t1, and a function π(ε1, ε2), possibly ϖ. They also mention an integral of f(ε1) dε1 taken along a cross-cut in T from ε1 to ε2 and equal to such a function π(ε1, ε2). This reads like notes on third-kind normal integrals with logarithmic points ε1, ε2, but it is too fragmentary to reconstruct with certainty.
errors: No mathematical error. The orientation convention is stated only loosely ('positive or negative side against the direction from inside to outside'). With the standard counterclockwise orientation, Green's theorem gives ∬(dY/dx - dX/dy), i.e. the negative of the integrand Riemann writes. He covers this with 'equal in the first case, opposite in the second', and the sign is irrelevant because the integrand is 0.
Implicit assumption: X and Y must be differentiable enough for Green's theorem; the page only states continuity. This is standard for the period and is also left implicit in the published version.

results.what: Closed-path integral of an exact (closed) 1-form over the full boundary of a region vanishes, via the area integral of dX/dy - dY/dx
results.modern_name: Green's theorem / Stokes' theorem in the plane; path independence for closed forms on boundaries
results.usually_credited_to: Green (1828), Gauss, Ostrogradsky; Cauchy for the complex-analytic analogue

results.what: Programme of analysis situs: path independence holds when every closed curve bounds, motivating simply vs. multiply connected surfaces
results.modern_name: Simple connectivity / first homology (Riemann's connectivity number)

results.what: Marginal fragment: integral along a cross-cut from ε1 to ε2 giving a function π(ε1,ε2) of two points, apparently related to third-kind integrals
results.modern_name: Abelian normal integrals of the third kind / reciprocity (tentative)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the draft of a well-known published section of Riemann's 1857 Abelian functions paper (Crelle 54), nearly verbatim. The marginal notes are fragmentary and concern standard parts of the same theory.

checkable.sympy: x,y,t=symbols('x y t'); X=-y/(x**2+y**2); Y=x/(x**2+y**2); simplify(diff(X,y)-diff(Y,x))
checkable.asserts: The form is closed (result 0) on the punctured plane, which is not simply connected.
Equals 2*pi: a closed curve that does not bound a part of the surface can give a nonzero integral, motivating the simple-connectivity hypothesis.
Equals 0: an exact form on a simply connected region has zero integral over a closed boundary curve.
Green's theorem check on the unit disk (define r,s as symbols first); result 0. This fixes the sign convention: with counterclockwise orientation the area integrand is dQ/dx - dP/dy.

transcription_corrections: Folio number at top right reads '135', not '35'.
Before 'und X, Y' the words 'Fläche T' are struck through; T is attached to the preceding line ('zusammenhängende Fläche T gegeben').
'überall im ersteren Falle gleich' – the image looks more like 'identisch im ersteren Falle gleich'; the published version has simply 'im ersteren Falle gleich, im letzteren entgegengesetzt'.
The struck word in 'Flächen[...]' is uncertain. The surviving word before ∫(...)dT appears to be 'Flächentheil'/'Flächenintegral'; the published text reads 'Flächenintegral'.

Right margin: 'mit der letzten und vor nächster Ordnung unendlich groß und unendlich kleinen Functionen' more plausibly reads 'nur der ersten und von erster Ordnung unendlich gross und unendlich kleinen Functionen'.
Right margin: the first struck line reads something like 'ergänzt werde' or 'eingesetzt werde' rather than 'ausgeführt werde'; uncertain.
Right margin: π(ε1,ε2) may be Riemann's ϖ; 'Unregelmässigkeiten' is doubtful (possibly 'Unstetigkeiten').
